facts.raw_span: 2 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness
difficulty combing her hair and rising from a chair
morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
dysphagia for solids and liquids
without fever or weight loss
symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs
brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
leukopenia (WBC 2.96 × 10^3/µL)
microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL)
elevated C-reactive protein (18.8 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (109.2 mm/hr)
bilateral sacroiliitis
bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement

concepts.why: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with JDM.
Suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and markedly elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies are consistent with thyroiditis.
Bilateral sacroiliitis is a characteristic finding in inflammatory conditions such as sacroiliitis.
Progressive proximal muscle weakness and bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement are consistent with myositis.
Overlap of musculoskeletal, rheumatologic, and endocrine features is consistent with MCTD.
Progressive proximal muscle weakness and bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement are consistent with polymyositis.
Progressive proximal muscle weakness and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with inflammatory myopathy.
Overlap of musculoskeletal and rheumatologic features is consistent with autoimmune myopathy.
Suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and progressive proximal muscle weakness are consistent with thyroid-associated myopathy.
Progressive proximal muscle weakness and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy.

rationales.F01: Progressive proximal muscle weakness is a key feature of inflammatory myopathies, such as Juvenile Dermatomyositis and Polymyositis.
rationales.F06: Symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs indicates significant muscle weakness, consistent with myopathic disorders.
rationales.F11: Bilateral sacroiliitis is a characteristic feature of Sacroiliitis and can be seen in other conditions such as Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, symmetric muscle strength reduction, and microcytic anemia support Juvenile Dermatomyositis, with Autoimmune Myopathy as a close alternative due to similar symptoms and evidence of autoimmune involvement.
